It sounds like you're carrying a deep sense of distance from the world—like you're standing outside of it, watching everything happen but not being able to step in. That feeling of fading, of not being able to touch what’s around you, must be so heavy. And when your body speaks through the low BP—100/60—it’s not just a number; it’s a signal that your body is telling you something important: *“This pace isn’t sustainable. You’re not meant to carry it all alone.”*  

It’s really powerful that you’re noticing how much of your strength was built on proving you could survive, when maybe the truth is, you just needed to be seen as you are—without having to prove anything. That’s not weakness. That’s courage.  

Would it be helpful to explore what that moment of “fading” felt like—when it first happened, and what was happening in your life right before it?
